subject: Mathematics

curriculum_expectations.B11.1: use directional and positional language to create and follow instructions involving movement
curriculum_expectations.B11.3: communicate and record step-by-step instructions using symbols, words, or pictures

unit_overview: A 5-day Kindergarten unit on foundational coding (B11.1-B11.3) framed around 'Little Programmers' — Bot the Robot Programmer and Buggy the Debug Beetle. Day 1 introduces DIRECTIONAL words (forward, back, left, right). Day 2 adds POSITIONAL words (above, below, beside, between). Day 3 records step-by-step instructions with symbols and pictures. Day 4 TESTS instructions and finds bugs. Day 5 closes with a Big Programmer Capstone integrating all 3 expectations. Each lesson includes an expanded_walkthrough.
unit_learning_goal: Children will use directional and positional words, record step-by-step instructions, and test/refine them.

lesson_arc.big_idea: DIRECTIONAL words tell us HOW TO MOVE: forward, back, left, right.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can use direction words to move.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Bot moves on a mat; children practice 4 direction words.

lesson_arc.big_idea: POSITIONAL words tell us WHERE: above, below, beside, between.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Bot hides; children describe with position words.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We RECORD steps with arrows and pictures so anyone can follow.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can record steps with pictures.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Bot records routes with arrow cards; children build picture codes.

lesson_arc.big_idea: TEST your code. If wrong, REFINE — find the BUG and fix it!
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can test and refine my steps.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Buggy points to bugs; children fix 4 broken codes.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Programmers MOVE, RECORD, and TEST step by step.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can move, record, and test instructions.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children rotate 4 stations: move, position, record, test.

recurring_characters.role: Lead character. Coding helper. Anchors all 5 lessons.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A friendly robot with a square body, arrow buttons on chest, and antennae shaped like question marks.

recurring_characters.name: Buggy the Debug Beetle

threaded_vocabulary.child_friendly_definition: IN THE MIDDLE of two things.
A MISTAKE in the code. We FIX bugs!

pedagogical_notes: Kindergarten coding is hands-on and physical — body movement first, paper second.
Directional and positional words OVERLAP — both are about WHERE.
Recording with arrows + pictures bridges to symbolic coding.
TEST + REFINE introduces debugging — celebrate finding bugs!
Use whole-body learning: walk the route before drawing it.
canadian_context_notes: Bot navigates a Canadian neighbourhood map.
Bug Cards include hockey puck targets.
Floor mat themes: Tim Hortons, library, park.
Object cards: maple leaf, beaver, hockey stick.
